feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy, web, and content leadership roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond platform scale, and could be streamlined by reducing overlap across competencies/skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression with increasing responsibility at one organization, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong relevance and scope: Drupal, analytics, governance, email, social, video, and AI-enabled search show breadth plus modern digital capability.  
- Generally clean, professional writing with good use of specifics such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: include results like traffic growth, engagement lifts, email performance, cost savings, team size, budget size, or efficiency gains—not just responsibilities and platform scale.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency fixes: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; keep serial comma usage consistent (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “content operations and enterprise web improvement”); “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, currently learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy leadership, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a more concise framing like “multi-channel digital programs.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that support complex content operations. Strong background in advocacy and public-sector communications, cross-functional stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible messaging.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated heavily in skills sections.
- The intro should avoid restating detailed channel lists already covered elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it feel more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital transformation strategy,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure; use mostly noun phrases and avoid mixing broad functions with tactical tasks.
- Consider a tighter version: Digital transformation strategy • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, insights & reporting • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- If space allows, prioritize the most current strengths: digital transformation, CMS/platform modernization, analytics, governance, and AI/search-related systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “data analytics & reporting” also overlap with Technical + IT and Analytics sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consulting impact, platform modernization, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and campaign delivery for member-facing communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcomes-oriented phrasing: “Designed and implemented…” / “Streamlined…” / “Led…” / “Improved…”; add metrics if available (site traffic, toolkit downloads, publishing speed, search success, stakeholder adoption).
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 stronger ones, e.g.:
- Led Drupal campaign builds, including microsites, modular storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved digital operations through analytics, workflow design, governance, and cross-channel communications standards.
- Directed AI-enabled search development, defining retrieval approach, structured content requirements, and discovery UX.
- Cut “technical troubleshooting” and “best practices” phrasing unless tied to a concrete result.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital systems, workflows and analytics” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- Microsites and AI search also duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and impact-focused.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Consolidate into 4–5 impact bullets, led by the website modernization: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add team size, budget, reporting improvements, production volume, cost savings, engagement growth, or turnaround-time reductions.
- Tighten softer bullets: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video series”; “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to strengthen decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless framed as scaling infrastructure, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but the item reads internally focused and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around execution leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scale: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy delivery across teams.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-oriented: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” If possible, add views, frequency, or audience growth.
- Replace vague workflow bullets with specifics: note publishing cadence, cross-functional teams supported, turnaround time reduced, or consistency gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing the program.
- “Improved workflows/editorial coordination” overlaps with the 2022–2024 role; keep this version tactical rather than governance-focused.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad terms with sharper, less repetitive language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel” to “Cross-channel” and “messaging” to “communications” for a more executive, systems-oriented tone.
- If space allows, make one line more distinctive to recent work, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms.”
- Keep this section capability-focused; save tools, AI, analytics, and platform specifics for other skills sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat language already used in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is close to experience bullets on storytelling/editorial coordination but is less differentiated than governance/operations language.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the separate “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills item, emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes over exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms (WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages) • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Drop “jQuery” from topline skills unless it is required for target roles; it feels dated and is better left in Technical + IT.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for large public-sector sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep this section strategic and let the technical section carry the full tool inventory.
- “Workflow automation” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies; avoid repeating exact phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI

- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent Director/Consultant work, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and slightly more strategic.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Reporting & Optimization**
- Replace with tighter phrasing: **GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • Analytics infrastructure and dashboard development • KPI framework design and executive/leadership reporting • SEO, user behavior and performance analysis**
- Group tools first, then capabilities; this improves scanability and signals both hands-on and leadership-level ownership.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one measurable proof point tied to recent work, e.g. **analytics stack supporting a 10,000+ page site / 3.5M annual page views** rather than listing more platforms.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization**; consider keeping tools there and making this section more strategic/capability-led.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in **Core Competencies**; avoid repeating that exact phrase.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either add specificity on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize recent, proven platforms first: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add proficiency/context rather than just names: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint; lightweight publishing: Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid mixing product list style here and broader capability language elsewhere.
- If this section is meant to be technical depth, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project or modern web publishing narrative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus broader capabilities.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles; repeating it without context adds little.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as a tighter, more senior-facing list: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required by the role; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or application in adjacent context, e.g., “for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation,” to connect tools to outcomes.
- Put the strongest/current differentiators first: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions, API integrations, then front-end languages.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Google Tag Manager may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” to reduce cross-category overlap.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since the CV already emphasizes automation and governance, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to group by function and emphasize implementation strength: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Drop Basecamp unless it was meaningfully used in recent roles; it feels older/less relevant than the rest.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” to better match the leadership narrative.
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of a pure list, e.g. “Airtable (workflow systems), Power Automate/Zapier (process automation), Jira/Asana/Trello (project operations), Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello overlap heavily; keep all three only if ATS coverage is a priority.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of current email/engagement capability. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, this item should feel more strategic and aligned to that work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/recency: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: **Higher Logic (member communications/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- Use consistent naming: either **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys** or **Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys**, but avoid the slash if possible.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters; keep this item tool-focused and leave audience scale/results in the experience section.
- “Engagement” may feel broad unless supported by CRM/automation language; consider “Email Marketing & Marketing Automation Platforms” instead.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts,” production volume, or workflow improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten scope and outcomes: “Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; improved publishing workflows during a major website refresh.”
- Clarify production impact with metrics if available: number of livestreams, cadence/length of weekly video series, audience growth, turnaround time, or team efficiency gains.
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations, improved publishing workflows during a major website refresh, and produced recurring digital content including livestreams and weekly video updates. Provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/producing the format, not expanding it.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; frame this as foundational support rather than leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and make the podcast line sharper and more outcome-oriented.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and initiative: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the multimedia line: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, translating research and program work into accessible formats.”
- Make the standout achievement more direct: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item more focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast first.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
